english_abstract: This paper investigates grant-free random access in low Earth orbit satellite Internet-of-Things systems without global navigation satellite system (GNSS) assistance. To accommodate large differential delays and Doppler shifts across devices in the absence of GNSS-assisted timing and frequency precompensation, we first propose a multi-frame affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) transmission scheme and analyze its input-output relationship. Building on this model, we learn a score-based generative prior for the AFDM effective channel without requiring a sparse representation or grid-aligned delay–Doppler parameters, using colored Gaussian perturbations during training to account for correlated estimation errors in the receiver. Subsequently, the learned prior is incorporated into a message-passing (MP) receiver for minimum mean-squared error (MMSE) denoising, providing posterior mean and variance estimates without explicit high-dimensional integration. These posterior moments are combined with soft activity probabilities obtained from a learned density-ratio estimator, thereby incorporating activity uncertainty into channel estimation. The resulting soft information is iteratively exchanged with a linear estimation module for joint activity detection and channel estimation (JADCE). Numerical simulations demonstrate that the proposed receiver outperforms the baseline receiver in activity detection and channel estimation.
